edition.alertText: Crude flows recover to 10.3M b/d (76% of pre-war) but Iran targets engine rooms — at least 23 ships hit in October; Munir arrives in Tehran for fifth mediation round

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 234 with crude flows partially recovering even as Iran intensified attacks on commercial shipping. Kpler data for the week to Saturday showed Gulf crude exports averaging approximately 10.3 million barrels per day — 76% of the 13.6 million bpd crude-only pre-war baseline — up sharply from 8.5 million bpd the prior week. However, refined product flows remain severely constrained at roughly 11% of total Hormuz cargoes versus over 20% pre-war, as Middle East refinery throughput stays depressed at 7.3 million bpd (down from 9.9 million in February). Bloomberg reported on October 20 that Iran has shifted tactics to targeting engine rooms of vessels, with at least 5 direct engine-room hits among the 23 vessels struck in the first two weeks of October. The IRGC also claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the strait — its 54th such claim since the war began — which CENTCOM has not confirmed.

Oil markets remain volatile with Brent pushing back above $110 per barrel. Brent traded near $110.05 on Wednesday, up 1.2% as Societe Generale strategists noted it had backed up to $111.2 — its highest since May 20. WTI held above $98.50, gaining after two sessions of declines and up over 10% month-to-date. The Brent-WTI spread widened to roughly $11 as Trump continued efforts to ease US fuel prices through Russia sanctions waivers. VLCC tanker rates remain near $1.3 million per day — 43 times the January level of $30,000 — with freight at approximately $33 per barrel, making up more than 27% of delivered crude cost versus 3% pre-war (Poten data). US diesel prices remain above $6 per gallon, with California at roughly $8.40. The G7 released 100 million barrels from emergency stocks on October 2 and the IEA released over 20 million barrels of diesel on October 15, but the US SPR has fallen to 283 million barrels — its lowest since 1982.

Diplomatic channels multiplied ahead of a potential post-midterms escalation. Pakistan's army chief Gen. Asim Munir arrived in Tehran on Tuesday evening for his fifth visit since the April ceasefire, accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, seeking to revive the stalled Islamabad MoU framework. Russia's Lavrov had visited Tehran on Monday — his first trip since the war began — meeting Araghchi and President Pezeshkian and proposing a regional collective security architecture. Qatar continues passing proposals between Washington and Tehran behind the scenes. However, Axios reported Defense Secretary Hegseth held an unannounced meeting with Netanyahu in Israel on Monday, and Trump has endorsed Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 election. An additional US aircraft carrier is expected in the region by late November. On supply chains, the FAO Food Price Index hit 136 points in September — its highest since November 2022 — as S&P Global warned that Hormuz energy shocks combined with El Niño are creating conditions for a global food crisis. Bangladesh reported fertilizer stocks falling below safe levels, with only two of five urea plants operating.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 45% from pre-war. Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — record highs. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. MEG supplied ~35% of global urea and 25% of ammonia.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Urea exports down 83%, ammonia down 75% vs pre-war (ITC data). Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain near zero. Bangladesh fertilizer stocks below safe levels — only 2 of 5 urea plants operating. FAO Food Price Index hit 136 in September (highest since Nov 2022). S&P Global warns of global food crisis as El Niño compounds supply shock.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: Qatar LNG exports down 95% from pre-war (ITC). QatarEnergy extended force majeure into November. Asia's JKM gas benchmark 51% above pre-closure levels. Global coal demand forecast to rise 1.2% to record 8.94B tonnes (IEA). Newcastle coal up 40% YTD at $150/t as Asian buyers switch from LNG.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint.
